postings.advert_text:
Research Fellow in Energy Geostructures

Heating and cooling of buildings is a key priority for global decarbonisation due to the scale of the demand and the current reliance on fossil fuels. Energy geostructures, where civil engineering substructures are connected to ground source heat pump systems offer a novel solution to this challenge. Appropriate design of energy geostructures requires consideration of the thermal behaviour and associated energy assessment. At the University of Leeds, our dynamic energy geotechnics team are leading research in this growing area. We would like to recruit someone to develop our research in design and analysis of diaphragm walls used for thermal energy extraction. Are you an ambitious researcher looking for a new challenge? Do you have expertise in ground energy systems and energy geostructures, especially their thermal analysis and design? Do you want to join an expanding research team at a leading UK university?

As part of an exciting EPSRC-FAPESP project, Efficient Ground Energy Systems in Diaphragm Walls in Challenging Conditions, led by Prof Fleur Loveridge, you will lead innovative research into the design and analysis of energy retaining walls used as ground heat exchangers. The project aims to encourage the adoption of energy retaining walls through provision of better guidance. It includes a mixture of laboratory and field scale testing and a range of computational techniques carried out across three Universities – University of Leeds, University of Dundee and University of Sao Paulo. In particular the project will:

Understand the impact of temporary and spatial variation in ground properties on heat transfer and stress/strain conditions in the walls;
Develop and test models of heat flow around the walls, as well as implement them for routine use;
Develop and test new approaches for geotechnical design for energy retaining walls.

As a Research Fellow in Energy Geostructures on this project you will lead research in delivering new knowledge on the thermal design and performance of energy walls to facilitate rapid implementation of embedded retaining walls for widespread application. You will:

Undertake numerical simulations of energy walls, and understand which modelling and ground condition simplifications are acceptable with reference to field data as appropriate;
Develop, test and implement analytical models for planar heat flow around energy walls;
Work closely with project partners at University of Sao Paolo and University of Dundee to integrate their inputs and outputs into your analysis;
Collaborate with other University of Leeds researchers on development of energy systems modelling tools for energy walls;
Take a leading role in production of project outputs including journal papers and accessible guidance for practice.

What we offer in return

26 days holiday plus approx.16 Bank Holidays/days that the University is closed by custom (including Christmas) – That’s 42 days a year!
Generous pension scheme plus life assurance– the University contributes 14.5% of salary
Health and Wellbeing: Discounted staff membership options at The Edge, our state-of-the-art Campus gym, with a pool, sauna, climbing wall, cycle circuit, and sports halls.
Personal Development: Access to courses run by our Organisational Development & Professional Learning team.
Access to on-site childcare, shopping discounts and travel schemes are also available.

And much more!

 The Faculty of Medicine at the University of Southampton invites applications for a three-year, full-time, fixed-term Research Fellow to join Professor Hanieh Yaghootkar’s interdisciplinary precision-diabetes research programme. Based at University Hospital Southampton, you will investigate the biological mechanisms underlying type 2 diabetes by integrating measures of organ health with large-scale genetic and clinical data. Working alongside genetic epidemiologists, clinicians and data scientists, you will apply advanced statistical and machine learning approaches to identify distinct diabetes subtypes, investigate their genetic determinants and improve prediction of disease risk and progression. 

 The role 

 As a Research Fellow, you will:

 Develop and apply machine learning approaches to identify distinct subtypes of type 2 diabetes using measures of liver, pancreas, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle health.

 Characterise the clinical, metabolic and genetic profiles of diabetes subtypes and evaluate their reproducibility across populations.

 Conduct genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of organ-health traits and diabetes subtypes, and apply Mendelian randomisation to investigate potential causal relationships.

 Develop and evaluate statistical and machine learning models to predict incident type 2 diabetes and disease progression using genetic and clinical data.

 Analyse large-scale population datasets, including UK Biobank, using robust statistical methods and reproducible computational workflows.

 Contribute to high-quality scientific publications, conference presentations and the dissemination of research findings.

 Collaborate with multidisciplinary researchers across genetic epidemiology, genomics, clinical medicine, imaging, statistics and data science.

 You will have opportunities to develop your research expertise, contribute to innovative analytical approaches and build your publication record within an internationally collaborative research environment. 

 About you 

 You will have:

 A PhD in in genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, biostatistics, data science, computational biology or a closely related discipline.

 Experience analysing large-scale genetic, epidemiological or biomedical datasets, ideally including UK Biobank.

 Strong statistical and computational skills, including proficiency in R and/or Python and experience working in Linux-based computing environments.

 Practical experience conducting GWAS and Mendelian randomisation analyses, including appropriate quality control, sensitivity analyses and interpretation.

 Experience applying machine learning, clustering, predictive modelling or other advanced statistical methods to complex biomedical data.

 An understanding of genetic epidemiology and the application of statistical methods to investigate complex disease mechanisms.

 Evidence of high-quality research outputs, including peer-reviewed publications.

 Excellent analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams.

 Experience with metabolic disease research would be advantageous.

 What we can offer 

 At Southampton, you will join a supportive, internationally connected research environment at the forefront of genetic epidemiology, data science and precision medicine. We offer:

 Access to large-scale biomedical datasets, high-performance computing infrastructure and secure analytical environments.

 Opportunities to work at the interface of human genetics, medical imaging, machine learning and metabolic disease research.

 Collaboration with leading researchers across clinical medicine, genomics, epidemiology and computational science.

 Opportunities for high-impact publications, scientific conferences, professional development and career progression.

 A supportive and inclusive working environment committed to equality, diversity and flexible working, including Athena SWAN principles.

 A competitive University benefits package, including pension provision and generous annual leave.

 For informal enquiries, contact Professor Hanieh Yaghootkar ( h.yaghootkar@soton.ac.uk ).

Birmingham City University is looking to appoint a high calibre graduate as an Advanced Research Engineer – Materials Technology, and Coatings (KTP Associate) to deliver an exciting 30-month Knowledge Transfer Partnership in the BCU’s Department of Management, Business and Marketing (Business School) and Department of Engineering (ABCE) and Hockley Mint Limited. 

This role presents an exciting opportunity to work in collaboration with leading academics at Birmingham City University, to apply knowledge and technical innovation, delivered on site at the company. 

This Knowledge Transfer Project (KTP) is co-funded by a grant from Innovate UK and Hockley Mint Limited. It is therefore essential you understand the fundamentals of the KTP collaboration between a UK business and a University works to deliver benefits for each (the company, the university, and the graduate) For more information please go to Home - Knowledge Transfer Partnerships

Personal Training & Development Budget: 

The KTP Associate will have access to a wide range of benefits including a personal development budget of £5,000 to upskill during the project. 

Location and Reporting:

The successful candidate will be employed by Birmingham City University and seconded to work full-time onsite at Hockley Mint Limited,70-71 Warstone Lane, Birmingham, West Midlands,B18 6NG.The KTP Associate will deliver the 30-month KTP project in partnership with Birmingham City University and Hockley Mint Limited.

The KTP Associate will be supervised and mentored by both a knowledge base lead and academic supervisor from BCU’s Department of Management, Business and Marketing (Business School) and Department of Engineering (ABCE),and by Hockley Mint’s Company Supervisor.

Hockley Mint Limited: 

Hockley Mint is a long-established Birmingham manufacturer that combines traditional jewellery craftsmanship with modern production technology. It serves jewellery retailers and brands with everything from bespoke one-off pieces to large-scale production runs, while maintaining a strong focus on British manufacturing and sustainable practices. For further information please visit One of Europe's largest jewellery manufacturers | Hockley Mint

The successful candidate will have full access to Birmingham City University’s resources such as offices, labs, and library to complete the KTP project (a project workplan written with KPIs and outcome deliverables has been written)

The KTP Associate will be expected to interact with the senior management, suppliers and clients of the company as well as BCU academics. 

Main Duties and Responsibilities: 

The KTP Associate will work on:

New alloy development based on experimental work including processing of materials (casting, thermo-mechanical processing etc) and coating (PVD deposition, electroplating and anodizing)
Testing and characterization of the developed materials including mechanical and optical response, chemical and corrosion testing and also biocompatibility. 
Assessing the sustainability of the new alloy systems, developing processes that embed circular credentials in the manufacturing and commercialization of the products. 
Developing a commercialisation document that will allow the company to implement a route to market plan
Developing project and milestone documents (presentations, risks registers, health and safety assessments)

The role requires the successful candidate to develop:

Technical documentation relating to the development of new alloy systems
Any additional health and safety documentation that may come out from the development of new alloy
A commercialisation plan to market the new alloy
A mini-product passport highlighting the sustainability characteristics of the developed alloy

The KTP Associate must also be adept at applying their knowledge to commercial projects, driving value and making an impact where possible, with an ability to solve problems and create innovative solutions.

The KTP Associate must have the following key attributes to ensure the project’s successful completion.

Skills and Experience: 

The KTP Associate will hold a relevant masters or PhD degree. 

Essential:

A minimum Master’s level qualification in material science, metallurgy or chemistry 
Excellent communication skills to express ideas effectively, orally, graphically and in writing to articulate complicated matters between the academics and the company project team members
An ability to work to tight deadlines with diligence, attention to detail, and maintain high standards of work
An ability and aptitude to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary team; and self-management and planning skills to make optimum use of time
Strong leadership skills in successfully implementing and embedding new innovations within a company or organisation

Desirable:

PhD in a related subject or relevant experience 
Academic acumen to enable successful reporting through 
research publications in academic journals and 
marketing/training materials
Practical experience of working in the field of metallurgy.

Personal Skills:

Enthusiastic, self-motivated and able to take a proactive role in delivering the proposal's work plan successfully
Practical interpersonal skills to establish good working relationships with colleagues, stakeholders, and industrial partners
Excellent communication skills to express ideas adequately and articulate complicated matters between the academics and the company project team members either orally or in writing
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and computational skills, along with being adept at applying knowledge to commercial projects, driving value and making an impact where possible
Strong project management skills

For further information please contact Michal.Krzyzanowski@bcu.ac.uk or arun.sukumar@bcu.ac.uk

Interviews will take place week commencing 4th January 2027.

About the role
As a Research Associate in Atmospheric Dispersion Modelling on the SENTINEL project, you will lead its physics-based dispersion modelling and validation work, helping to develop a new approach to forecasting chemical fugitive emissions. You will set up and run established atmospheric dispersion models, including ADMS, the Met Office NAME model and CALPUFF, to provide scientific benchmarks for SENTINEL's AI forecasts. You will prepare meteorological and geospatial inputs, design hindcasting experiments and evaluate forecast performance against health guideline categories and community odour reports. Working closely with the project's AI Research Associate, you will also assess whether predictions are physically plausible and contribute to explainable AI analysis and guidance for regulators and public health agencies.
You will join an interdisciplinary team in the School of Engineering, working across atmospheric science, AI, chemical fate and public health and collaborating with partners including the UK Health Security Agency and the Met Office. The project also has links with the University of Leicester's Institute for Environmental Futures, which brings together interdisciplinary research addressing environmental challenges and the relationships between environment and human health. This is an opportunity to contribute to high-quality research with practical applications, disseminate findings through publications and conferences, develop collaborations and help shape research at the intersection of atmospheric modelling, AI and public health.
About you
You will have a PhD, equivalent professional qualification or equivalent experience in atmospheric science, meteorology, environmental science or engineering, physics, applied mathematics or a related discipline. You will bring experience or demonstrable ability in the physical modelling of environmental processes, together with strong analytical problem-solving skills and evidence of contribution to peer-reviewed publications or equivalent technical outputs. Experience of an atmospheric dispersion model such as NAME, CALPUFF or ADMS is important, although candidates with a strong physics-based or numerical environmental modelling background and the ability to become proficient with these tools quickly are also encouraged to apply.
You will be able to use Python and/or R for scientific data processing, analysis and visualisation, and communicate complex information effectively to a range of audiences. You will be comfortable working both independently and collaboratively, including with internal and external stakeholders, and will bring a commitment to developing your expertise and contributing positively to a collegiate research environment. Experience with weather or geospatial data, AI or machine learning, high-performance computing, air-quality guidance, or hands-on use of NAME, CALPUFF or ADMS would be advantageous.
Additional information

Informal enquiries are welcomed and should be directed to Dr Timothy Pearce at tcp1@leicester.ac.uk

As part of the University’s ongoing commitment to professional development, this role will also be considered on a seconded basis for existing staff members. Please ensure this is discussed with your line manager prior to applying. More information regarding secondments can be found here.
 
The University of Leicester has been changing the world, and changing people’s lives, for 100 years. When you join us, you’ll become part of a community of Citizens of Change, which includes not only our staff and our current students but also thousands of Leicester graduates around the world.
 
As a diverse and forward-thinking employer, we embed the principles of equity, diversity and inclusion into everything we do. That includes not just our core missions of teaching and research, but also our support for staff, students and our local community through our values of Inspiring, Impactful and Inclusive through our values of Inspiring, Impactful and Inclusive.
 
We’re committed to the wellbeing of all our staff and to the sustainability of our environment, on our campus and beyond. We offer a competitive salary package, excellent pension scheme and a generous annual leave allowance, along with opportunities to develop your career in a supportive and collaborative environment.

About the Role  

About the Role

The School of Engineering and Materials Science at Queen Mary University of London is looking for a Research Assistant (RA) to join the "Self-Learning AI Recipe Engine" project, carried out in collaboration with an agri-tech industry partner.

 The project explores how AI, computer vision, and reinforcement learning can optimise growing conditions in indoor vertical farming. Under the guidance of Dr M Hasan Shaheed, the successful candidate will help develop and test AI models using crop images and sensor data.

 The role will involve preparing and labelling datasets, supporting the training and evaluation of computer vision models for tasks such as plant growth monitoring, and assisting with reinforcement learning models that recommend growing conditions.

This position offers an opportunity to gain experience across AI, data analysis, computer vision, and controlled-environment agriculture within a collaborative research setting.

This is a full-time, 12-month position.

About You

We welcome applications from candidates with an MSc in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Data Science, or a closely related subject.

You should have some experience working with machine learning in Python, ideally using tools such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, and an interest in applying AI to real-world challenges. Experience with computer vision, image analysis, and preparing datasets for machine learning projects would be beneficial.

We are looking for someone who is comfortable working with data, evaluating model performance, and applying statistical techniques to analyse results. The candidate will also contribute to experimental trials at the industry partner's growing facility, help analyse results, and support the preparation of research publications.

 Experience with reinforcement learning, sensor data, or agricultural applications of AI would be an advantage, but is not essential.

About the School

The School of Engineering and Materials Science (SEMS) is a large, research-intensive School within the Faculty of Science and Engineering, comprising over 110 academic staff and a vibrant community of approximately 2,700 undergraduate and taught postgraduate students, alongside more than 250 PhD researchers. The School offers a dynamic and interdisciplinary research culture, ranked 7th overall in the UK for research excellence in REF2021, and 2nd nationally for world-leading research outputs.

About Queen Mary

At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable.

Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers.

We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form.

Benefits

We offer competitive salaries, access to a generous pension scheme, 30 days’ leave per annum (pro-rata for part-time/fixed-term), a season ticket loan scheme and access to a comprehensive range of personal and professional development opportunities. In addition, we offer a range of work life balance and family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements, and campus facilities.

Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for any candidate with a disability. We are open to considering applications from candidates wishing to work flexibly.

Research Catalyst Fellow in Audio

The Institute of Sound Recording (IoSR) is seeking a high-potential postdoctoral researcher to join us as Research Catalyst Fellow, strengthening the IoSR’s research and external funding (fixed term up to Oct 2028). This role offers the opportunity to build your research profile while helping the Institute develop ambitious research programmes, secure external funding and produce high-quality outputs and meaningful impact.

Working closely with the IoSR’s academic staff across its research areas in audio and acoustic engineering, and with our industry and academic partners, you will develop research ideas into competitive proposals, identify opportunities and help build the consortia needed for collaborative bids. 

A substantial part of the role will involve developing and coordinating competitive proposals for funding bodies such as the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), Horizon Europe, and industry. You will proactively identify external funding opportunities that advance the IoSR’s research priorities and help colleagues develop fundable programmes of work. Working alongside colleagues, you will make substantive intellectual and methodological contributions, from shaping research questions and study designs to generating pilot evidence and writing applications. Through substantive roles in collaborative projects and, where appropriate, fellowship applications, you will develop a sustainable, externally funded research portfolio that supports your academic development and the IoSR’s research ambitions. Proposals that leverage AURORA³, the IoSR’s new national strategic infrastructure for audio, acoustics and AI research, are expected to form part of this portfolio. 

Alongside your collaborative research responsibilities, you will have protected time for research you lead. This will support the development of your research profile and publication pipeline in leading journals and conferences, complemented by opportunities to contribute to publications arising from collaborative projects. 

You will hold a PhD in engineering, computer science, acoustics, or a related area by the appointment start date and bring strong methodological skills, a promising publication record or pipeline, and the ability to develop rigorous research ideas and persuasive proposals. We are looking for a proactive and collegial researcher who can work effectively across disciplines and build productive relationships with academic colleagues and external partners.

Your research will address questions in audio and acoustic engineering with applications in areas such as immersive media, communications, consumer audio and hearing health. We welcome expertise across signal processing, spatial audio, psychoacoustics, and machine learning for audio.

About the Institute of Sound Recording (IoSR)

The Institute of Sound Recording (IoSR) at the University of Surrey is an internationally leading centre for research in psychoacoustic engineering, combining acoustics, auditory perception, signal processing and machine learning. The IoSR is also home to the world-renowned Tonmeister degree in Music and Sound Recording, which has produced a stream of highly successful graduates who have collectively received numerous accolades, including three Oscars, twelve Grammys, six Emmys, and twelve BAFTAs.

Please complete the application form on the Surrey portal and attach your CV with full list of publications, and a short cover letter explaining why you are interested in the role.

About the role

Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Sustainable Polymer Chemistry to work with Professor Matthew Davidson, in collaboration with academic and industrial partners, for a period of up to 2 years. The post is supported by the EPSRC through the Sustainable Chemicals and Materials Manufacturing Hub (SCHEMA, www.schemahub.ac.uk) which aims to deliver a step change in sustainable chemical and polymer manufacturing in the UK.

The project focusses on sustainable catalysis for the preparation of new plastics based on ring-opening polymerization, ring-expansion polymerization and polycondensation of renewable monomers. Highly selective and robust catalysts will be designed and investigated to deliver controlled polymer architectures resulting in materials with desired properties for commodity and high value applications. 

You will join a dynamic team of other experts working in polymerization catalysis and polymer chemistry at Bath and, as a member of the SCHEMA Hub, you will benefit from collaborations across UK universities and with companies. Applicants should have a PhD in Polymer Chemistry with experience of polymerization catalysis prior to taking up the post. Experience of catalyst and polymer characterization techniques, including spectroscopy, GPC, DSC, TGA and tensile mechanical measurements is required.

Role Description

We welcome applications from skilled and motivated researchers to design and develop experimental cryogenic fuel research facilities.

About the Role

This role will lead the design, development and operation of novel fuel experimental research facilities. The postholder will act as a primary contact for rig build, safety assurance and day-to-day operation of complex high pressure/temperature experimental rigs supporting research projects.

About You

You will be educated to PhD level (or be nearing completion thereof). You must have experience of experimental rig design and development, including control, instrumentation and data acquisition systems. You will be able to demonstrate knowledge of health and safety practices, including risk assessments, COSHH, and safe operation of high-risk facilities involving electrical systems and pressurised or flammable gases. You will have a proven ability to work autonomously, maintain research documentation, and provide leadership within a laboratory or test-rig environment.

About Us

As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield’s world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here.

The Centre for Aeronautics, Propulsion and Power, within the Faculty of Engineering and Applied Sciences, has an established international reputation in gas turbine propulsion and power plant research, as well as aircraft design, aerodynamics and flight control. Its activities span performance simulation, diagnostics, advanced cycles, engine control, combustion, and low-emission technologies, supported by extensive participation in UK and EU-funded programmes and longstanding industrial partnerships. The Opportunity:

Help us redefine what’s possible. Be part of something bigger. 

 

The School of Informatics is seeking a Senior Researcher to develop AI for Science methods specialised to quantum computing. You will join the Quantum Software Lab and work with Professor Elham Kashefi, colleagues across the University of Edinburgh, and researchers in the UK quantum-computing community.

The central research question is how AI systems can take part in scientific work while remaining open to inspection and expert judgement. The remit includes systems that help researchers find and formulate hypotheses, connect scientific literature to software and experiments, use specialist tools, assess evidence, and record how a conclusion was reached. Relevant methods may come from agentic AI, neuro-symbolic systems, formal methods, language models, knowledge representation, data infrastructure or scientific software engineering. The post-holder will have scope to shape the methods and research questions pursued.

The immediate setting is a UK programme on AI-enabled quantum science. Work already under way at Edinburgh includes AI Pathfinder, which searches for useful connections across the quantum software and hardware literature, and an agent harness for research, verification and review. These are starting points rather than limits on the role. You may also work on evaluation, reproducibility, provenance, human oversight, integration with scientific models and tools, quantum computing hardware, or new approaches that arise from collaboration with quantum researchers.

 

You will:

Lead the design and implementation of research software and experimental studies.

Define evaluation methods for AI-assisted scientific work, including failure analysis and comparison with expert judgement.

Work with quantum researchers to turn broad questions into assessable computational investigations.

Publish and present the resulting research and release software or research artefacts where appropriate.

Coordinate technical work with project partners and support junior researchers.

Contribute to future research proposals and the wider development of the Quantum Software Lab.

 

You will have a PhD, or equivalent research experience, in computer science, artificial intelligence, quantum information, mathematics, physics or a related field. You will have evidence of independent research and the ability to design, implement and evaluate substantial computational work. That evidence may span theoretical computer science, systems and software engineering, data and knowledge systems, or computational work in fields such as biology and medicine. We value candidates who can move between theory and implementation, learn the language of a new field, and transfer methods across disciplinary boundaries. Clear writing and sound software practice are essential.

Experience in one or more of agentic AI, machine learning, formal methods, knowledge representation, scientific computing, open research infrastructure or research software engineering would be useful. Experience of quantum computing is welcome. We also encourage applications from researchers with an unusual or varied disciplinary path who can show how their work transfers to quantum science.

 Help us redefine what’s possible. Be part of something bigger.  

 The School of Informatics is seeking a Senior Researcher to develop AI for Science methods specialised to quantum computing. You will join the Quantum Software Lab and work with Professor Elham Kashefi, colleagues across the University of Edinburgh, and researchers in the UK quantum-computing community.

 The central research question is how AI systems can take part in scientific work while remaining open to inspection and expert judgement. The remit includes systems that help researchers find and formulate hypotheses, connect scientific literature to software and experiments, use specialist tools, assess evidence, and record how a conclusion was reached. Relevant methods may come from agentic AI, neuro-symbolic systems, formal methods, language models, knowledge representation, data infrastructure or scientific software engineering. The post-holder will have scope to shape the methods and research questions pursued.

 The immediate setting is a UK programme on AI-enabled quantum science. Work already under way at Edinburgh includes AI Pathfinder, which searches for useful connections across the quantum software and hardware literature, and an agent harness for research, verification and review. These are starting points rather than limits on the role. You may also work on evaluation, reproducibility, provenance, human oversight, integration with scientific models and tools, quantum computing hardware, or new approaches that arise from collaboration with quantum researchers.

 You will: 

 Lead the design and implementation of research software and experimental studies.

 Define evaluation methods for AI-assisted scientific work, including failure analysis and comparison with expert judgement.

 Work with quantum researchers to turn broad questions into assessable computational investigations.

 Publish and present the resulting research and release software or research artefacts where appropriate.

 Coordinate technical work with project partners and support junior researchers.

 Contribute to future research proposals and the wider development of the Quantum Software Lab. 

 You will have a PhD, or equivalent research experience, in computer science, artificial intelligence, quantum information, mathematics, physics or a related field. You will have evidence of independent research and the ability to design, implement and evaluate substantial computational work. That evidence may span theoretical computer science, systems and software engineering, data and knowledge systems, or computational work in fields such as biology and medicine. We value candidates who can move between theory and implementation, learn the language of a new field, and transfer methods across disciplinary boundaries. Clear writing and sound software practice are essential.

 Experience in one or more of agentic AI, machine learning, formal methods, knowledge representation, scientific computing, open research infrastructure or research software engineering would be useful. Experience of quantum computing is welcome. We also encourage applications from researchers with an unusual or varied disciplinary path who can show how their work transfers to quantum science.

Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) is a distinctive, unique institution, rooted in the Liverpool City Region and with a global presence. Our students and staff, past, present, and future, are the beating heart of our city and can be found in every corner of every industry and community. We couldn’t exist anywhere else and have shaped the city in which we belong. Working with the people of Liverpool to improve lives and support communities is at the heart of why we were founded and why we exist today.

The School of Education is pleased to invite applications for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join an exciting new research project focused on supporting children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD often referred to as dyspraxia) in educational settings.

We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled researcher to undertake this full-time fixed term appointment for 18 months. You will contribute to research investigating how children with DCD/dyspraxia can be better supported in the classroom and how educational resources can be made more accessible.

The post forms part of ‘Lab2School4All’ – an innovative five-year EU Horizon funded project that aims to improve the accessibility of school resources for children with DCD/dyspraxia. Research has shown that many children with DCD/dyspraxia present with persistent challenges related to handwriting and visuospatial organisation, which can create barriers to learning. Working with partners across five countries, the project team will be conducting a range of focus groups, interviews, and targeted experimental studies to explore how primary-aged children with DCD/dyspraxia access and use adapted versions of school textbooks. The findings will inform the development of practical resources and recommendations for AI-based tools that can adapt educational materials for use in mainstream classrooms and specifically create an AI-powered open-source platform designed to automate the adaptation of primary school textbooks. Overall, the project has significant potential for impact in improving accessibility and inclusive education for children with DCD/dyspraxia.

You will support the delivery of the ‘Lab2School4All’ strand based at Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU). A key focus of the LJMU team is to investigate effective writing accommodations for children with DCD/dyspraxia. You will lead the recruitment of participants, manage data collection and analysis, and contribute to a predominantly quantitative study evaluating the effectiveness of different accommodations, including handwriting, typing, and speech-to-text. As part of the study, you will administer standardised assessments of motor skills (e.g., the Movement Assessment Battery for Children, third edition) alongside cognitive and literacy measures. You will also conduct interviews with children to explore their experience of using these different writing accommodations.

Additional responsibilities will include coordinating research timelines and project meetings, supporting collaboration with project partners in Ireland, France, Italy and Spain, and contributing to the wider management of the project. A unique element of this post is the potential collaboration with other postdoctoral researchers in the partner institutions. The role will also involve dissemination activities, including the preparation of peer-reviewed publications, funder reports, conference presentations, social media engagement, and updates to the project website.

In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction, and development support as well as family-friendly policies.

This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do. Find out more about working at LJMU here.

If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you.

Informal enquiries can be directed to Dr Emma Sumner: e.j.sumner@ljmu.ac.uk 

We would encourage applications from all individuals who meet the advert criteria, but would particularly encourage applications from women, ethnically diverse groups, LGBTQ+ groups; and disabled people. The University is proud of its commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion and endeavours to cultivate a staff base that is representative of society. Please let us know if you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process.

Please note all of our vacancies will be closed to applications at midnight on the advertised closing date, unless otherwise stated.

 NTU researchers are global leaders in river ecology. To ensure the real-world relevance of our research, we work with a breadth of external partners. We are seeking to recruit a grade E Research Assistant and grade F Research Associate to join our team to contribute to the ‘Headstart’ project with collaborators at Freshwater Habitats Trust, Wessex Rivers Trust and the Environment Agency.

 These posts are within the burgeoning discipline of river restoration. The project aims to advance understanding of how ‘winterbourne’ chalk streams—ecosystems recognized for their biodiversity, including rare and specialist species—respond to restoration actions. Enabled by our collaborators, we will collect new field data to extend our previous characterization of physical habitats, and aquatic and terrestrial invertebrate communities. These new data will create a uniquely valuable dataset bringing new insight into the effectiveness of restoration actions.

 Research Assistant 

 Working alongside a grade-F Research Associate, your role will be to collect new field data, then to process invertebrate samples and identify the taxa present. You’ll also have opportunities to contribute to analysis and reporting, as we prepare to share findings with our research community. You’ll also have opportunities to join stakeholder meetings, strengthening your professional network.

 Research Associate 

 Working alongside a grade-E Research Assistant, your role will be to organize and lead field trips, then to process the collected invertebrate samples and identify the taxa present. You’ll also lead the analysis of the resultant dataset, and work alongside the project leader to prepare to share findings with our research community. You’ll also have opportunities to join stakeholder meetings, strengthening your professional network.

 Both roles 

 We welcome applications from candidates who have scientific understanding of river ecosystems and experience of using keys to identify aquatic and/or terrestrial invertebrates, as well as experience using R to analyse ecological data.

 For more details, please see the supporting documents. We'll consider applications even if you don't meet every one of the requirements, so don't be put off if you don't match them perfectly. Recognizing the diverse needs of our team we are open to discussing flexible working patterns, whilst meeting project requirements.

 The School of Science and Technology at Nottingham Trent University (NTU) is an exciting multidisciplinary environment for learning, teaching and research, with some of the best facilities in the UK.

This mix of traditional and modern subjects encourages and inspires future innovators.

 Research in the School underpins the teaching of our courses and is highly interdisciplinary by nature. Everything we do has a real-world impact on society, and provides significant contributions to scientific knowledge, advanced research training and opportunities for commercial exploitation.

We enable high performing research teams and future research leaders to thrive and make an impact locally, regionally, nationally, and globally.

 The Research Fellow will contribute to the UKRI-funded H2R project at Coventry University’s Centre for Agroecology, Water and Resilience (CAWR), focusing on developing and testing a portable greywater and rainwater treatment and reuse system.

About us 

The Department of War Studies is one of the only academic departments in the world focused on understanding the complex realm of conflict, security, and international politics through inter-disciplinary teaching, research and engagement. We have a large and diverse faculty, with varied theoretical and methodological expertise in areas including, but not limited to, conflict resolution, contemporary and historical warfare, gender, international relations, migration and borders, security studies, strategic studies, technology and violence. 

The Department is located within the School of Security Studies and the Faculty of Social Science & Public Policy. Together, we are committed to embedding good diversity and inclusion practice into all of our activities. We are committed to encouraging further growth in our diversity, and we look forward to welcoming applicants of all abilities and backgrounds, whom we are able to support with our flexible varied working practices. Overall, King’s values the diversity of its staff and student body and recognises that this is both a strength and a defining feature of King’s as a London university in a global context.

About the role 

The Department of War Studies seeks to appoint a Research Fellow for the ERC Nuclear Echoes Project (led by PI Dr Nicola Leveringhaus, funded by ERC Consolidator Grant 101229981).

The successful candidate will work closely with the PI and wider project team, taking day-to-day responsibility for leading and delivering Work Package 1 which will design and develop a global nuclear weapons commemoration database. Working closely with the PI and wider project team, the postholder will develop the conceptual and methodological foundations of the database, establish shared data-collection rules, engage in and support related fieldwork across the project, and produce academic and public-facing research outputs. An experimental launch of the database is planned in 2029.

In terms of expected outputs, beyond the database, at least one peer-reviewed academic article (can be single authored or co-authored with the PI) is expected on the database, for example on the methods and/or release of the database. The Research Fellow is also expected to assist  other team members in curating a Special Issue for the project. Given long publishing time-frames, the peer-reviewed publications need only be submitted/ideally accepted for publication within the time-frame of the role 

In this role, the Research Fellow will present findings at internal workshops, as well as international conferences, including organising a panel or roundtable where appropriate, and publish shorter briefs or blog posts as opportunities arise. The Research Fellow will work closely with the PI and colleagues across the project’s other work packages, ensuring that Work Package 1 supports the project’s wider comparative research. They will also take part in the collaborative life of the project, including monthly team meetings, any relevant seminars and project workshops, and related activities of the CSNS and CNSS research centres where possible.

This post is a three-year full-time fixed-term research role ideally starting on 1 January 2027.

About the role
We are seeking a Research Associate in International Space Law to join the Leverhulme Centre for Humanity and Space (LCHS), based at Space Park Leicester. The Centre brings together interdisciplinary research across the Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences to develop new insights into humanity’s relationship with space, with researchers working alongside physical scientists, space companies, businesses and governmental bodies. You will undertake a research project in international space law, with particular interest in the responsibility of private actors under international law for activities in outer space. Potential areas of investigation include environmental protection, sustainable space exploration, space resource utilisation, property rights and related international litigation. This complements the University’s wider international space law research, which examines the legal frameworks governing space activities by states and private entities.
You will take responsibility for developing and delivering your research, including collecting and analysing data, developing theoretical approaches or empirical analysis, and disseminating findings through appropriate academic and public outputs. The opportunity is particularly suited to an early career researcher seeking to develop their own research profile within an interdisciplinary environment.

Closing Date: 19 November 2026 

 

 

 

The Role

 

We are excited to launch this new opportunity for a Clinical Research Associate in Rheumatology and Dermatology to join us in the Faculty of Medical Sciences to work on the COMBAT-PsA experimental medicine investigation into psoriatic arthritis (PsA).

 

PsA is a chronic inflammatory arthritis affecting an estimated 0.3-1% of the general population and up to 30% of people with psoriasis. While targeted disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) – including those targeting IL-17 – have revolutionised the management of PsA, most patients fail to achieve low disease activity or long-term disease control; this is particularly the case for those living with obesity. Recent trial data suggests drugs shown to be effective in treating obesity via glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) may themselves have a beneficial therapeutic effect on PsA disease activity, The successful applicant will help deliver a multi-centre, prospective, longitudinal experimental medicine study deploying an IL-17 inhibitor and a GLP-1RA as “molecular scalpels” for evaluating tissue and peripheral molecular signatures associated with weight loss and immunomodulation in obese people with PsA,

 

This post provides a unique opportunity for an ambitious clinician to develop a practical understanding of experimental medicine research in Rheumatology and Dermatology, The Clinical Research Associate (CRA) will be responsible for delivering the aforementioned study but will also have opportunities to contribute to other early phase and experimental medicine trials and explore their own research interests.

 

You will join a diverse community of colleagues spanning the Musculoskeletal Disease and Inflammation Medicine and Skin, Oral and Immunogenomics Themes of the NIHR Newcastle Biomedical Research Centre. Contributing to our world-leading translational research programme. Based in the William Leech Building of Newcastle University’s Medical School, your clinical work will take place across Newcastle Hospitals, including the NIHR Newcastle Clinical Research Facility. (NCRF). You will play a central role in the team undertaking this important experimental medicine study, acting as a liaison between the research laboratory team, the NHS rheumatology/dermatology teams and the NCRF. The postholder will be responsible for identifying potential participants via face-to-face and telephone consultations, explaining the study to them, and obtaining consent. You will develop skills in minimally invasive skin, joint and adipose biopsy techniques. You will also have responsibility for local study management and logistics, including oversight of study visits, preparing study reports and manuscripts. We have a well-staffed laboratory infrastructure and there may also be the possibility to develop laboratory skills, dependent on further funding.

 

You will hold a medical degree, General Medical Council registration and a license to practice in the UK. You are a dynamic, conscientious, self-motivated team player, with a thirst for new knowledge and an appetite for discovery. This post is funded for one year but will provide an excellent platform for a research fellowship, potentially leading to a higher degree, depending on the successful candidate. You will work closely with various members of our collaborating teams, particularly Dr Arthur Pratt, to whom informal enquiries can be made

 

The post is fixed term for a period of 12 months

 

For informal enquiries contact NIHR Newcastle BRC MIM Theme Co-Lead Dr Arthur G Pratt.

 

 

To apply, please upload an up-to-date CV and letter of application outlining specific examples around how you meet the requirements set out in ‘The Person’ section below.

 

Interviews are expected to be held in November 2026.

 

Please note that before commencing in the role, an Honorary Contract pre-employment check will be required.

About the Role

Applications are invited for an exciting Postdoctoral Research Assistant position investigating how the Type VI Secretion System (T6SS) enables the enteric pathogen Campylobacter jejuni to compete, colonise and interact with the host. This project will uncover how T6SS-associated virulence effectors shape bacterial fitness, microbial competition and innate immune responses within the intestine. The successful candidate will combine molecular microbiology and infection biology with advanced avian and human intestinal models, including 2D/3D culture systems and organ-on-chip technologies, to uncover mechanisms of pathogen adaptation and persistence in physiologically relevant environments.

About you

We are seeking an ambitious and highly motivated researcher with a strong interest in bacterial pathogenesis and host–microbe interactions. The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

A PhD (or near completion) in Immunology, Infection Biology, Microbiology, or a related discipline
Strong research experience in bacterial pathogenesis, host–pathogen interactions, molecular microbiology, or infection biology
Practical expertise in bacterial infection models and molecular microbiology techniques
Knowledge of innate immunity, microbial competition, bacterial secretion systems, or virulence mechanisms
Experience with intestinal epithelial models, organoids, 3D culture or organ-on-chip systems would be advantageous
The ability to drive independent research, analyse complex data, communicate findings clearly, and contribute effectively to a collaborative research environment

About the School/Department/Institute/Project

 The project will be based within the William Harvey Research Institute (WHRI), an internationally recognised centre for research in immunity, inflammation, infection, and disease mechanisms. The host laboratory combines microbiology, immunology, and bioengineering to investigate bacterial pathogenesis, microbial competition, and host defence in the intestinal environment.

The project will involve access to advanced microbiology, cell culture, flow cytometry, imaging, and organ-on-chip technologies, together with collaboration with the Enterics Research Team at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM). This provides an interdisciplinary environment spanning microbial pathogenesis, intestinal biology, mucosal immunology, and infection research.

Job Title:  Research Associate in Biomedical Engineering
Posting Start Date:  06/11/2026

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

 

Are you a passionate researcher eager to bridge the gap between advanced engineering and clinical practice to tackle a transformative healthcare challenge? We have an exciting opportunity in the School of Mechanical, Aerospace and Civil Engineering for a Research Associate to apply their skills in biomedical engineering to revolutionize haemodialysis and make a profound impact on global health.

 

You will join the Thermofluids Group at the University of Sheffield, working in close collaboration with experts in the School of Medicine and Population Health and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals. As a key member of this interdisciplinary project, you will lead the design, assembly, and clinical validation of a novel dialyser prototype.

 

You will be responsible for testing the prototype using blood-mimicking fluids and, ultimately, human blood to assess cleaning efficiency, clotting risk, and biocompatibility.

 

This role offers a unique opportunity to apply fundamental engineering principles to real-world physiological conditions. You will work in close collaboration with two other Research Associates focusing on numerical simulations and experimental fluid dynamics, contributing directly to a greener, more efficient future for nephrology.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

 

Lead the assembly of the prototype, ensuring tight tolerances for spinning components, robust sealing, and integration of semi-permeable membranes. You will troubleshoot technical issues during assembly to ensure the prototype is ready for testing.
Conduct rigorous solute removal efficiency tests using Human Peripheral Simulated Blood Plasma (BZ464). You will measure the clearance rates of key metabolites, including urea, creatinine, and phosphate, to optimize the operational parameters of the dialyser.
Manage the ethical procurement and testing of voluntarily donated human blood to assess biocompatibility. You will evaluate the prototype for fibrin strands, check transmembrane pressure, and analyse blood samples for clotting and haemolysis markers, ensuring safety standards are met.
Work closely with the fluids engineering PDRAs to translate simulation and experimental results into physiological insights. You will actively participate in weekly meetings with renal clinicians at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals to interpret data and refine the device design based on clinical feedback.
Maintain meticulous records of experimental methodologies and results in compliance with clinical governance frameworks. You will contribute to the writing of high-impact journal publications, present outcomes at international medical and engineering conferences, and participate in public engagement events regarding sustainable nephrology.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post.

 

Person Specification

Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. Please ensure that you reference the application criteria in the application statement when you apply.

This will consist of a candidate’s presentation on their background and research experience and an interview. A small tour of the campus will also be given, where possible. Swansea University is a research-led university that has been making a difference since 1920. The University community thrives on exploration and discovery and offers the right balance of excellent teaching and research, matched by an enviable quality of life.

Our stunning waterfront campuses and multicultural community make us a desirable workplace for colleagues from around the world. Our reward and benefits, and ways of working enable those who join us to have enriching careers, matched by an excellent work-life balance.

We are seeking to appoint an enthusiastic and self-motivated Research Assistant to join our team to work on studies focusing on primary and emergency care.  As part of the PRIME Centre Wales collaboration funded by Health and Care Research Wales, we use a range of quantitative and qualitative approaches to study models and treatments to improve patient outcomes, avoid unnecessary contacts, and streamline the emergency care system.  We have a strong international reputation in the field and established collaborations with health service and academic colleagues across the UK and internationally.

 This post offers the opportunity to join an exciting new research project at University College London (UCL) investigating how scattering processes and detector interactions affect the measurement and extraction of integrated intensities in electron crystallography. The aim is to optimise the measurement and integration of electron diffraction data to deliver more accurate structural results.

 Funded by the BBSRC award “Closing the data-quality gap for serial crystallography and electron diffraction”, the project marks the commencement of a new collaboration with Diamond Light Source and the STFC maintainers of DIALS and CCP4. The research will combine the development of a theoretical model of electron diffraction with the construction of a digital twin of the experiment. The resulting methods will be implemented in DIALS.

 The appointee will be part of a collaborative team spanning UCL and Harwell with opportunities to spend time at Harwell working directly with project partners. They will also share responsibility for designing and maintaining the group’s research software supervising undergraduate and postgraduate researchers contributing to future funding proposals and leading the preparation of research publications.

 The appointee will have a PhD (or near completion) in physics, chemistry, materials science or a related discipline, with a strong background in crystallography, electron microscopy, or theoretical modelling of scattering/diffraction. A strong understanding of the principles of crystallography and diffraction, and in-depth knowledge of either electron microscopy/diffraction or the theory of scattering processes (e.g. electron or X-ray scattering, wave optics or related physics) are required.

 The appointment is for a fixed term of 36 months, starting as soon as possible. The candidate will join the Advanced Microscopy and Crystallography Lab led by Dr Andrew Stewart in the Department of Chemistry at the Bloomsbury Campus of University College London. Information about the group can be found at https://amclab.github.io
